title: KV cache consistency & retention — architecture review notes (2026-06-15)
summary: Notes from the architecture review focused on KV cache consistency and retention policies. We reviewed the RFC for TTL tiers, eviction strategies, version-aware keys, and rollout plan. Outcome: agree on a hybrid TTL+LRU policy with model-version namespacing, soft-ttl refresh for hot keys, per-tenant caps, and a staged canary rollout with additional metrics and alerts.
decisions: Adopt hybrid retention policy: TTL tiers + LRU eviction within per-shard/per-tenant caps.
Include model-version in KV cache key namespace to enable safe model rollouts and explicit invalidation.
Implement a 'soft-ttl' refresh path for top-k hot keys to proactively refresh in background to reduce first-token latency for hot prefixes.
Default TTLs: 1 hour for generation prefixes, 24 hours for short embeddings cache. Allow per-tenant overrides through runtime config and feature flags.
Canary rollout: start at 5% traffic on 2026-06-22, increase to 25% after 72 hours if metrics stable, full rollout target week of 2026-06-29.
Add SLI/SLO guards: increase in first-token latency >5% or cache hit-rate drop >10% triggers automatic rollback to previous config.
Prioritize key-versioning and metrics before canary release; do not enable soft-ttl by default until canary passes.
discussion_notes:
Recap and motivation:
- Ava opened with RFC goals: reduce cache-induced stale outputs during model rollouts, limit memory footprint growth, and keep first-token latency within SLOs.

Consistency and model rollouts (Ethan):
- Problem: serving runtime routes to different model variants during rollouts; cached KV entries generated by older variants can produce outdated continuation behavior. We discussed two options: global invalidation on rollout or version-aware keys. Global invalidation is simple but expensive and unsafe at scale. Versioned keys are cleaner and allow co-existence during canaries.
- Agreement: use model-version prefix added to KV keys (e.g., model:v2::prefixhash). This simplifies invalidation and reduces blast radius.

Retention / TTL proposals (Priya):
- Proposed TTL tiers: short (15-60m) for generation prefixes, medium (6-24h) for embeddings & long-lived session caches. Also proposed per-tenant cap to prevent noisy neighbors.
- Concerns: very short TTLs increase miss rate, long TTLs increase memory. Tradeoff to tune per workload.

Eviction strategy and latency (Liam):
- LRU is simple and well-understood, but LFU gives better retention for bursty workloads. We agreed on LRU within each shard combined with an admission policy that favors new prefixes only if they pass a lightweight hotness filter. Also discussed maintaining a small frequency sketch for eviction decisions; decided to defer heavy-weight LFU sketches for later.
- Discussed eviction-induced 99th percentile tail latency when evicting large prefix entries; mitigation: evict in background and avoid blocking inference threads, cap per-eviction work. Also implement async prefetch for expired hot keys (soft-ttl).

Soft-TTL refresh strategy:
- Implement background refresh for keys with high QPS. Refresh is asynchronous and judged safe because model-version namespacing prevents mixing results across rollouts. Refresh should fail closed: if refresh fails, continue serving stale or miss based on policy.

Per-tenant caps and quotas:
- Agree per-tenant memory caps enforced at shard-level and a soft degrade mode for tenants that exceed cap (lower cache admission rate rather than hard eviction). We will expose tenant-level metrics for debugging.

Monitoring and metrics (Zoe):
- Metrics required before canary: global and per-tenant cache hit-rate, miss-rate, first-token latency P50/P95/P99, memory usage per shard, number of key-version mismatches, soft-ttl refresh success/failure rates.
- Alerts: hit-rate drop >10% over 15m, first-token latency P99 increase >5% over baseline, memory >85% of capacity for >10m.

Rollout plan (Miguel):
- Plan: gated feature flags. Stage 1 (dev): run in staging with synthetic load. Stage 2: canary 5% production traffic (2026-06-22). Stage 3: increase to 25% after 72h if metrics stable. Stage 4: full rollout after additional verification. Rollback via feature flag.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to choose good defaults for TTL across workloads? (Action: run retrospective analysis on production prefix reuse patterns).
- Cost tradeoffs for background refresh vs extra calls to model endpoints.
- Implementation complexity for per-tenant admission policies vs global admission policy.

Meeting end: reconvene for follow-up on metrics and key-version PR reviews.
